{{short description|French physicist and nanosciences specialist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2026}}
[[File:Jacqueline Bloch.jpg|thumb|Jacqueline Bloch in her laboratory at Centre de Nanosciences et de Nanotechnologies (C2N), Univ. Paris Saclay]]
'''Jacqueline Bloch''' (born 1967) is a French physicist, specialist in [[Nano sciences|nanosciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.lpn.cnrs.fr/fr/Commun/PagePersonnelle.php?nom=Bloch&prenom=Jacqueline |title=Sa page personnelle sur le site du LPN |access-date=7 February 2020 |archive-date=22 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170922195242/http://www.lpn.cnrs.fr/fr/Commun/PagePersonnelle.php?nom=Bloch&prenom=Jacqueline |url-status=dead }}</ref> She is known for her research on [[polariton]] condensates.

== Biography ==
Jacqueline Bloch is the daughter of physicist [[Claude Bloch]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Jacqueline Bloch, magician of light |url=https://news.cnrs.fr/articles/jacqueline-bloch-magician-of-light |access-date=17 September 2026 |website=CNRS News |language=en}}</ref> She graduated as an [[ESPCI Paris|ESPCI]] engineer in 1991 (106th promotion), with a DEA in [[condensed matter physics]] (1990). She holds a [[doctorate]] from the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] on the study of the optical properties of quantum wires.<ref>{{SUDOC|043924719|nu=}}</ref> In 1994, she joined the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] and carried out her research at the L2M (Laboratoire de microstructures et de microélecroniques) in [[Bagneux, Hauts-de-Seine|Bagneux]], which moved and became the LPN (Laboratoire de photonique et nanostructures) in [[Marcoussis]] in 2001. In 1998, she spent a year there and carried out research at the [[Bell Labs|Bell Laboratories]]. 

Bloch is interested in the ultimate coupling between light and matter in close connection with [[semiconductor]] [[Nanotechnology|nanotechnologies]]. In particular, she has made important discoveries in the study of the physics of [[polariton]] condensates.

In 2026, Bloch represented the Academy of Sciences as a member of the commission to develop a list of [[List of names on the Eiffel Tower#Criticism|72 women in STEM]] proposed to be added to the 72 men named on the [[Eiffel Tower]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://cdn.paris.fr/presse/2026/02/03/88f01a14fc58f5500063be529bf4e6fe.pdf |title=72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel |date=2026 |publisher=Femmes et sciences association |pages=93}}</ref>

She has two sons, also scientists.<ref name=":1" />

== Awards ==
* 2014: Chevalier of the [[Legion of Honour|Légion d'Honneur]]<ref>{{Légifrance|base=JORF|numéro=PREX1415111D|texte=Décret du 11 juillet 2014 portant promotion et nomination}}.</ref>
* 2015 : [[Jean-Ricard Prize]] of the [[Société Française de Physique|French Physical Society]]<ref>[https://www.sfpnet.fr/laureate-du-prix-jean-ricard-2015-jacqueline-bloch Jacqueline Bloch, lauréate 2015 du prix Jean Ricard]</ref>
* 2017: [[CNRS Silver Medal]]<ref>[http://www.cnrs.fr/fr/recherche/prix/medaillesargent.htm Médaille d'argent 2017: les lauréats]</ref>
* 2019: [[Ampère Prize|Prix Ampère]] de l'Electricité de France of the French Academy of Sciences<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Laureats/prix-ampere-2019-jacqueline-bloch.html|title=Prix Ampère|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>
* 2019: Elected member of the French Academy of Sciences<ref>{{cite web|title=Communiqué de presse de l'Académie des sciences du 19 décembre 2019 : "Dix-huit nouveaux membres élus à l'Académie des sciences"|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/communique/elections_2019.pdf|website=www.academie-sciences.fr|date=19 December 2019|access-date=9 January 2020}}</ref> in the Physics Section.
* 2026: [[CNRS Gold Medal]]<ref name="y779">{{cite web | title=La Médaille d'Or du CNRS 2026 remise à Jacqueline Bloch | website=Académie des sciences | url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/la-medaille-dor-du-cnrs-2026-remise-jacqueline-bloch | language=fr | access-date=17 September 2026}}</ref>
